title: Ahlul Bayt and Their Authority — Part 637

sentences.en: This statement is unfortunate, coming as it does from a man like Ibn Abi'l-Hadid.

All sensible people
would object to it.
But surely Allah is All-Just and All-Wise.

He does
not give preference to an inferior man and let him supersede a more deserving person.

Allah says in the Holy Qur'an,
"Say: Are those who know and those who do not know alike?"

(39:9)
Again He says: "Is then he who guides to truth more worthy to be followed or he who himself goes not
aright, unless he is guided."
Ibn Abi'l-Hadid clearly admits that ‘Ali was the man who most deserved the caliphate.

He says in his
Sharh al-Nahju'l-Balagha, v.I.

p.4: "Verily, ‘Ali was superior to all mankind after the Holy Prophet of
Allah.
Regarding the matter of the caliphate, he was the most deserving of all the Muslims."

"City of knowledge" proves ‘Ali’s right to be the first caliph
Moreover, the Holy Prophet's explicit statement at the conclusion of this hadith confirms ‘Ali's superiority:
"He who is desirous of seeking knowledge must come to the door."

So is this portal of guidance whom the Prophet has ordered us to seek more worthy or he whom the
people have chosen?
